note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see edge/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: RF Industries added brand-new deferred-tax-asset release language to its Q2 FY2026 10-Q MD&A that is absent from the Q1 10-Q filed three months earlier — 'it is reasonably possible that a reduction of a significant portion of the valuation allowance may be appropriate in a future reporting period', with 'cumulative losses' recast into the past tense ('In prior periods, the Company recorded a valuation allowance due primarily to cumulative losses') — against a $4,521,000 allowance which on 11,424,572 diluted shares is roughly $0.40 per share of potential one-time GAAP EPS, versus a $0.18 two-analyst consensus.

The -52% slide from the 16 July 2026 peak of $21.50 to $10.27 has no disclosed company-specific cause: EDGAR's full filing history for CIK 0000740664 shows the last 8-K of any kind was 2026-06-15, with nothing since except an ARS/DEF 14A on 2026-07-28, a routine 13G on 2026-07-29 and a 13G/A on 2026-08-14 — no S-3, no shelf takedown, no 424B, no prospectus supplement, and Form 4 activity only in the company's own recurring quarterly cluster (13 Jan, 14 Apr, 14 Jul).

findings.finding: COMEX copper ran at or near all-time highs through the whole of RF Industries' fiscal Q3 (1 May - 31 July 2026), printing a record $6.83/lb in August and sitting at $6.47/lb on 11 September, +41.2% over twelve months — against a business where custom cabling (37% of H1 FY2026 sales) plus interconnect (35%) is 72% of revenue and where the bar management set is a record 35.1% gross margin it called sustainable above $20m of quarterly revenue.

findings.finding: The published FY2026 revenue consensus of $28.72m requires H2 revenue of $15.11m (~$7.55m per quarter) against an H1 actual of $13.61m (~$6.81m per quarter), and the Marine Technology segment that has to deliver it printed $2.71m and $2.84m in Q1 and Q2 FY26 against a $4.0m year-ago Q3 comp — it would need a 14-18% sequential jump to a segment already running -19% for the half.

The Middle East/Asia softness management called on 15 June 'not structural, it is a timing issue' that would 'resume swiftly' once pressure was alleviated instead escalated through the exact 1 May - 31 July fiscal Q3 window: the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to commercial traffic since 28 February 2026 and traffic slumped again in July on renewed US-Iran fighting and a blockade.

Coda Octopus has issued zero order or contract-award press releases in the sixteen months since 13 May 2025, against a prior cadence of three in ten weeks (a $1.3m engineering order 26-Mar-2025, a $1.4m engineering order 24-Apr-2025, a $1.5m DAVD order 13-May-2025) — and every one of its seven 2026 releases is an earnings or earnings-call item — despite the CEO telling investors on 15 June that 'we expect to see some orders in our third quarter' for DAVD following the Approved-for-Navy-Use designation.

findings.finding: CoinShares' own US ETF (BRRR) 10-Q puts bitcoin at $58,391 on 30 June 2026 vs $87,650 on 31 Dec 2025 (-33.4%) and BRRR net assets down 32.3% despite net creations, so group gross AUM of $7.4bn at FY2025 falls to roughly $5bn at 30 June; at the disclosed blended 170bp yield that is ~$50m of H1 asset-management revenue against $126.4m for FY2025, i.e. an annualised run-rate that turns the 3.0x trailing P/E screeners still display on CSHR into roughly 12x.

Capital Markets - 37% of FY2025 revenue and gains ($73.1m) but 44% of segment EBITDA ($57.7m of $131.3m) - is the one line that cannot be reconstructed from the monthly AUM CoinShares publishes, and its largest single component was disclosed as ETH staking at $4.3m in Q2 2025 alone, a line that scales with token price and with a futures basis that compressed through a half in which industry ETP AUM fell from ~$160bn in May to ~$141bn by 1 June on record outflows.

The lock-up agreed at listing expires 1 October 2026 - 12 trading days after this print - and the day after the print shareholders vote on a 2026 Equity Incentive Plan with an 11% initial pool plus up to 3% a year for 2027-2029 (up to ~20% of the 131.8m shares outstanding), while a co-founder/director's 10b5-1 plan starts selling in September and adds 1.5m shares of monthly diversification sales the moment the lock-up lifts.

Bitcoin is ~$78,800 on 8-10 September against the $58,391 close on 30 June that this release will report AUM at - a 35% recovery after the balance-sheet date - and the EGM the next morning asks for authority to buy back up to 25% of shares at $0.01-$20.00, giving management both a strong current-AUM update and a live capital-return lever to pair with a weak historical half.

Richard Nash has signed as 'Interim Chief Financial Officer' since the 20-F certification dated 30 April 2026 and is still 'Interim CFO' in the 8 September results notice - over five months with no permanent CFO named - while the company's own governance page lists him without the qualifier, and CoinShares issued no press release at all between 1 May and 21 July 2026 before publishing a release whose purpose was to confirm it would report quarterly.

findings.finding: A quiet 8-K filed 2026-04-17 (never press-released, absent from the company's own IR news feed) discloses a '2026 Retention Plan' with a $5,000,000 pool — roughly 9% of the ~$54m equity market cap — to keep executives 'during the pendency of the Company's strategic review process', vesting on the earlier of December 31, 2026 or 'certain milestone events or transactions'; that vest date is nine days after the December 22, 2026 debt maturity, which dates the board's own expected resolution to year-end rather than to this print, and makes the FY2027 guidance the CFO conditioned on 'completion of our strategic review' unlikely to appear on 2026-09-14.

The Nasdaq minimum-bid 180-day compliance date is 2026-09-21 — five business days after this print — and the cure the company itself named in the 8-K ('propose a reverse stock split to shareholders at its 2026 annual meeting') cannot complete in time, because Hain's annual meeting is held in early November (the 2025 meeting's item 5.07 8-K was filed 2025-11-05) and no PRE 14A or DEF 14A has been filed as of today; the only listing outcomes actually available in the week of the print are a transfer down to the Nasdaq Capital Market for a second 180 days, or a delisting determination.

The binding financial covenant is the 2.00:1.00 minimum interest coverage ratio, not the 5.50:1.00 maximum net secured leverage ratio the CFO points to ('leverage of 4.3x... plenty of headroom under the covenant of 5.5x'): interest and other financing expense ROSE to $45.1m for the nine months to 2026-03-31 from $38.4m a year earlier despite a $101m term-loan paydown, because the September 2025 Fourth Amendment raised the Term SOFR margin from 3.00% to 4.00%, while the TTM adjusted EBITDA implied by the company's own disclosed ratios fell from about $138m at 2025-06-30 to about $118m at 2026-03-31 — putting coverage near 2.0-2.3x against a 2.00x floor at the June 2026 test date being reported on Monday.

The -20.65% five-day run-in has no informational cause I could locate: no 8-K of any item since 2026-05-11, no company press release since 2026-08-17, and HAIN is NOT among the ten S&P SmallCap 600 deletions announced 2026-09-04 effective 2026-09-21 — so the de-rate into the print is positioning and forced supply, not news, in a stock last reported 13.9% short.
